z-m-39-01.title: Different values fit get the same total?
z-m-39-01.topic: Meaning of function and one-to-one function: sum condition for values and size of codomain
z-m-39-01.goal: Use counterexample to check that one-to-one function meaning (different elements get different values) no tell anything about sum of values. Explain that existence of function with same condition depend on codomain.
z-m-39-01.material: Think of function f from domain X={1, 2, 3, 4} to codomain Y={1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7} as value table. Table list only f(1), f(2), f(3), f(4) (no formula). Condition (가): f one-to-one, meaning different X elements match different values. Condition (나): f(1)+f(4)=f(2)+f(3). Mina say, “If one-to-one, all four values different. Then two pair sums no fit be equal like (나).”
z-m-39-01.thinking.0: Turning the claim into a value table and testing am
z-m-39-01.thinking.1: Making different examples (counterexamples) wey meet the conditions
z-m-39-01.thinking.2: Deciding if such function fit exist when codomain change
z-m-39-01.prereq.0: Meaning of function, domain, codomain, range and one-to-one function (first part of high school common mathematics functions unit)
z-m-39-01.prereq.1: Counting number of elements in a set
z-m-39-01.prereq.2: (School sequence note: H2 for this task na difficulty label assigned during production; we assume learner already study prerequisites above.)
z-m-39-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose your first judgment about Mina statement. (You no need calculate yet.)
z-m-39-01.s.s1.hint.0: Think of f(1), f(2), f(3), f(4) as four empty spaces and put four different numbers inside.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.hint.1: With the numbers you enter, write f(1)+f(4) and f(2)+f(3) separately, then compare if equal.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.o.a: Correct. If all four values different, the two pair sums too different.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.r.a: You treat “values are different” and “sums are different” like same statement. Choose two pairs yourself and compare the sums.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.o.b: Correct. One-to-one function increase as x increase, so the sums cannot be equal.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.r.b: You treat one-to-one and increasing function as same. Think whether one-to-one function fit have decreasing values.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.o.c: Wrong. Even if all values different, sums of two different pairs fit be equal.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.r.c: You read the claim as “always” and doubt whether example fit exist. Now check whether you really fit make one.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.o.d: We no fit decide. Na because formula for f no dey.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.r.d: You think of function only as formula. Here, table with four values enough to test the conditions.
z-m-39-01.s.s1.explain: One-to-one condition only say the four values different. Whether two pair sums fit equal even though values different, you must check by finding an actual example. Make we test next.
z-m-39-01.s.s2.prompt: Use value table to make 2 functions f wey meet both (가) and (나) and get f(1) bigger than f(2). The two functions must use different value sets. (a=f(1), b=f(2), c=f(3), d=f(4); all integers 1 to 7)
z-m-39-01.s.s2.hint.0: First find four different numbers wey make f(1)+f(4) equal f(2)+f(3).
z-m-39-01.s.s2.hint.1: Arrange the four numbers so f(1) bigger than f(2), then check again the two sums still equal.
z-m-39-01.s.s2.hint.2: Find another group of numbers, different from the first function numbers.
z-m-39-01.s.s2.ok.c1: All four values must belong to codomain Y (integers from 1 to 7).
z-m-39-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Every value must be integer from 1 to 7.
z-m-39-01.s.s2.ok.c2: All four values different, so this na one-to-one function.
z-m-39-01.s.s2.fail.c2: You use the same value two times. E no be one-to-one function.
z-m-39-01.s.s2.explain: Example, (3, 1, 6, 4) get 3+4=7=1+6 and all four values different. So Mina claim no hold. Also, since one example get f(1)>f(2), one-to-one function no always move toward bigger values. ((1, 2, 3, 4) meet sum condition but no meet f(1)>f(2), so no accept for this step.)
z-m-39-01.s.s3.prompt: New info: domain stay X={1, 2, 3, 4} and conditions (가),(나) same, but codomain Y change like below. Choose all codomains where function f fit meet the conditions. (No f(1)>f(2) condition.)
z-m-39-01.s.s3.hint.0: For each codomain, choose four different numbers, divide dem into two pairs, and write each pair sum side by side.
z-m-39-01.s.s3.hint.1: If codomain get fewer than 4 elements, first check whether one-to-one function fit exist at all.
z-m-39-01.s.s3.r.a: You think having 5 elements plenty. Choose four, split into two pairs, then check yourself if any pair sums fit equal.
z-m-39-01.s.s3.r.b: You check not just number of elements but also say numbers dey evenly spaced. Check whether you find pairs with equal sums.
z-m-39-01.s.s3.r.c: If you check sum condition first, easy to miss say elements no reach. First count how many values one-to-one function need.
z-m-39-01.s.s3.r.d: You check if codomain same size as domain fit get two pairs with equal sums. You consider case where all four numbers used.
z-m-39-01.s.s3.explain: {1,2,3} get only 3 elements, so the four X elements no fit get different values; one-to-one function no fit exist. {1,2,3,4} get 1+4=2+3, and {2,5,8,11,14} get pairs like 2+14=5+11. {1,2,4,8,16} get 5 elements but no two different pairs get equal sum. Plenty elements alone no enough; the actual numbers matter.
z-m-39-01.s.s4.prompt: Explain to Mina. Write (1) where original claim wrong with number example, and (2) show using codomain that function with same conditions no always exist.
z-m-39-01.s.s4.hint.0: Take one table you make in step 2 as is and write four values and two sums.
z-m-39-01.s.s4.hint.1: Choose a codomain you no choose in step 3 and write one sentence why function no fit be made with that codomain.
z-m-39-01.s.s4.selfAssess.0: Your number example clearly show four values all different and two pair sums equal?
z-m-39-01.s.s4.selfAssess.1: Did you separate wetin “one-to-one” tell us from wetin e no tell us?
z-m-39-01.s.s4.selfAssess.2: Did you give examples (too few elements or no equal-sum pairs) to show function fit or no fit exist depending on codomain?
z-m-39-01.s.s4.model.0: Four different values still fit get equal sums. For example, if f(1)=3, f(2)=1, f(3)=6, f(4)=4, all values differ and 3+4=1+6=7. But if codomain na {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}, wey get no two pairs with equal sums, you no fit make such function.
z-m-39-01.s.s4.model.1: One-to-one function only mean values no overlap; e no mean sums different. If f(1)=2, f(2)=1, f(3)=4, f(4)=3, then 2+3=1+4=5, so sums equal. But if codomain get only 3 elements, one-to-one function no fit exist at all. So whether function fit exist depend on codomain set.
z-m-39-01.s.s4.modelNote.1: E no mention if values increase, but get counterexample and output-set condition.
